--- file:///.src/failCauseToConstructor.ts ---
// @effect-v3
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics failCauseToConstructor:warning
import * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import * as Channel from "effect/Channel"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Exit from "effect/Exit"
import * as FiberId from "effect/FiberId"
import { pipe } from "effect/Function"
import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"
import { die as causeDie, fail as causeFail } from "effect/Cause"
import { failCause, failCauseSync } from "effect/Effect"

class AppError {
  readonly _tag = "AppError"
}

declare const error: AppError
declare const defect: unknown
declare const cause: Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, AppError>
declare const compute: () => number
declare const makeCause: () => Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const log: (message: string) => void

// MUST TRIGGER: defect cause (issue example) -> Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const crashed = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))

// MUST TRIGGER: typed failure cause (issue example) -> Effect.fail("not found" as const)
export const missing = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail("not found" as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy typed failure (issue example) -> Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))
export const lazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.fail(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier arguments -> Effect.fail(error) / Effect.die(defect)
export const failIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const dieIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST TRIGGER: side-effecting argument; both forms evaluate it eagerly -> Effect.die(compute())
export const dieComputed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(compute()))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect -> Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late")) (v3 has Effect.dieSync)
export const lazyDie = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyBlock = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: function-expression thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(function() { return error })
export const lazyFunction = Effect.failCauseSync(function() {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized inner constructor call -> Effect.fail(error)
export const parenthesized = Effect.failCause((Cause.fail(error)))

// MUST TRIGGER: explicit type argument on the inner constructor -> Effect.fail<AppError | string>(error)
export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: named imports resolve to the same APIs (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = failCauseSync(() => causeFail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: const alias of the API keeps its identity (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.fail(error))
const failCauseAlias = Effect.failCause
export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator
export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested in a function with an explicit Effect return type
export const withReturnType = (): Effect.Effect<never, AppError> => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: adjacent transformations in an existing flow -> Effect.fail(error)
export const transformationPair = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: replacing the flow prefix keeps later transformations
// -> pipe(Effect.die(defect), Effect.asVoid)
export const pipePrefix = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause, Effect.asVoid)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyFunctionPipe = pipe(() => Cause.fail(error), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.dieSync(() => defect)
export const lazyDiePipe = pipe(() => Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk body is itself a flow ending in Cause.fail -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyPipedBody = Effect.failCauseSync(() => pipe(error, Cause.fail))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already the direct APIs
export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const directFail = Effect.fail(error)
export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call
const storedCause = Cause.fail(error)
export const fromStoredCause = Effect.failCause(storedCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
export const sequential = Effect.failCause(Cause.sequential(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))
export const parallelLazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.parallel(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the constructed cause is transformed before being failed with
export const transformed = Effect.failCause(Cause.map(Cause.fail(error), (e) => e._tag))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Cause.fail and Effect.failCause are not adjacent in the flow
export const nonAdjacent = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Cause.map((e) => e._tag), Effect.failCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Cause constructors have no single-call Effect equivalent here
export const interrupted = Effect.failCause(Cause.interrupt(FiberId.none))
export const emptyCause = Effect.failCause(Cause.empty)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: type assertion on the argument changes the inferred error type
export const asserted = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error) as Cause.Cause<AppError | string>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type argument on failCause; with Cause.die it widens the
// error channel, which Effect.die(x) would not preserve
export const outerTypeArgumentDie = Effect.failCause<AppError>(Cause.die(defect))
export const outerTypeArgumentFail = Effect.failCause<AppError | string>(Cause.fail(error))
export const outerTypeArgumentPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause<AppError>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: return type annotation on the thunk pins the cause type
export const annotatedThunk = Effect.failCauseSync((): Cause.Cause<AppError | string> => Cause.fail(error))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause
export const lazyForwarded = Effect.failCauseSync(() => cause)
export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk does more than return the constructed cause
export const lazyMultiStatement = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  log("failing")
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: failCause of other modules (Exit, Stream, Channel) is not Effect.failCause
export const exitFailCause = Exit.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const streamFailCause = Stream.failCause(Cause.die(defect))
export const channelFailCause = Channel.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined APIs with the same names
const Local = {
  failCause: <E>(c: Cause.Cause<E>) => Effect.failCause(c),
  Cause: {
    fail: <E>(e: E): Cause.Cause<E> => Cause.fail(e),
    die: (d: unknown): Cause.Cause<never> => Cause.die(d)
  }
}
export const localFailCause = Local.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseFail = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseDie = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.die(defect))

// @effect-v3
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics failCauseToConstructor:warning
import * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import * as Channel from "effect/Channel"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Exit from "effect/Exit"
import * as FiberId from "effect/FiberId"
import { pipe } from "effect/Function"
import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"
import { die as causeDie, fail as causeFail } from "effect/Cause"
import { failCause, failCauseSync } from "effect/Effect"

class AppError {
  readonly _tag = "AppError"
}

declare const error: AppError
declare const defect: unknown
declare const cause: Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, AppError>
declare const compute: () => number
declare const makeCause: () => Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const log: (message: string) => void

// MUST TRIGGER: defect cause (issue example) -> Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const crashed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(new Error("boom")))

// MUST TRIGGER: typed failure cause (issue example) -> Effect.fail("not found" as const)
export const missing = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail("not found" as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy typed failure (issue example) -> Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))
export const lazy = Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier arguments -> Effect.fail(error) / Effect.die(defect)
export const failIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const dieIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST TRIGGER: side-effecting argument; both forms evaluate it eagerly -> Effect.die(compute())
export const dieComputed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(compute()))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect -> Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late")) (v3 has Effect.dieSync)
export const lazyDie = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyBlock = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: function-expression thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(function() { return error })
export const lazyFunction = Effect.failCauseSync(function() {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized inner constructor call -> Effect.fail(error)
export const parenthesized = Effect.failCause((Cause.fail(error)))

// MUST TRIGGER: explicit type argument on the inner constructor -> Effect.fail<AppError | string>(error)
export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: named imports resolve to the same APIs (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = failCauseSync(() => causeFail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: const alias of the API keeps its identity (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.fail(error))
const failCauseAlias = Effect.failCause
export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator
export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested in a function with an explicit Effect return type
export const withReturnType = (): Effect.Effect<never, AppError> => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: adjacent transformations in an existing flow -> Effect.fail(error)
export const transformationPair = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: replacing the flow prefix keeps later transformations
// -> pipe(Effect.die(defect), Effect.asVoid)
export const pipePrefix = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause, Effect.asVoid)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyFunctionPipe = pipe(() => Cause.fail(error), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.dieSync(() => defect)
export const lazyDiePipe = pipe(() => Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk body is itself a flow ending in Cause.fail -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyPipedBody = Effect.failCauseSync(() => pipe(error, Cause.fail))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already the direct APIs
export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const directFail = Effect.fail(error)
export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call
const storedCause = Cause.fail(error)
export const fromStoredCause = Effect.failCause(storedCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
export const sequential = Effect.failCause(Cause.sequential(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))
export const parallelLazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.parallel(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the constructed cause is transformed before being failed with
export const transformed = Effect.failCause(Cause.map(Cause.fail(error), (e) => e._tag))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Cause.fail and Effect.failCause are not adjacent in the flow
export const nonAdjacent = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Cause.map((e) => e._tag), Effect.failCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Cause constructors have no single-call Effect equivalent here
export const interrupted = Effect.failCause(Cause.interrupt(FiberId.none))
export const emptyCause = Effect.failCause(Cause.empty)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: type assertion on the argument changes the inferred error type
export const asserted = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error) as Cause.Cause<AppError | string>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type argument on failCause; with Cause.die it widens the
// error channel, which Effect.die(x) would not preserve
export const outerTypeArgumentDie = Effect.failCause<AppError>(Cause.die(defect))
export const outerTypeArgumentFail = Effect.failCause<AppError | string>(Cause.fail(error))
export const outerTypeArgumentPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause<AppError>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: return type annotation on the thunk pins the cause type
export const annotatedThunk = Effect.failCauseSync((): Cause.Cause<AppError | string> => Cause.fail(error))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause
export const lazyForwarded = Effect.failCauseSync(() => cause)
export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk does more than return the constructed cause
export const lazyMultiStatement = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  log("failing")
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: failCause of other modules (Exit, Stream, Channel) is not Effect.failCause
export const exitFailCause = Exit.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const streamFailCause = Stream.failCause(Cause.die(defect))
export const channelFailCause = Channel.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined APIs with the same names
const Local = {
  failCause: <E>(c: Cause.Cause<E>) => Effect.failCause(c),
  Cause: {
    fail: <E>(e: E): Cause.Cause<E> => Cause.fail(e),
    die: (d: unknown): Cause.Cause<never> => Cause.die(d)
  }
}
export const localFailCause = Local.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseFail = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseDie = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.die(defect))

// @effect-v3
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics failCauseToConstructor:warning
import * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import * as Channel from "effect/Channel"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Exit from "effect/Exit"
import * as FiberId from "effect/FiberId"
import { pipe } from "effect/Function"
import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"
import { die as causeDie, fail as causeFail } from "effect/Cause"
import { failCause, failCauseSync } from "effect/Effect"

class AppError {
  readonly _tag = "AppError"
}

declare const error: AppError
declare const defect: unknown
declare const cause: Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, AppError>
declare const compute: () => number
declare const makeCause: () => Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const log: (message: string) => void

// MUST TRIGGER: defect cause (issue example) -> Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const crashed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(new Error("boom")))

// MUST TRIGGER: typed failure cause (issue example) -> Effect.fail("not found" as const)
export const missing = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail("not found" as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy typed failure (issue example) -> Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))
export const lazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.fail(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier arguments -> Effect.fail(error) / Effect.die(defect)
export const failIdentifier = Effect.fail(error)
export const dieIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST TRIGGER: side-effecting argument; both forms evaluate it eagerly -> Effect.die(compute())
export const dieComputed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(compute()))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect -> Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late")) (v3 has Effect.dieSync)
export const lazyDie = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyBlock = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: function-expression thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(function() { return error })
export const lazyFunction = Effect.failCauseSync(function() {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized inner constructor call -> Effect.fail(error)
export const parenthesized = Effect.failCause((Cause.fail(error)))

// MUST TRIGGER: explicit type argument on the inner constructor -> Effect.fail<AppError | string>(error)
export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: named imports resolve to the same APIs (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = failCauseSync(() => causeFail(error))

export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator

  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const directFail = Effect.fail(error)
export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call
const storedCause = Cause.fail(error)
export const fromStoredCause = Effect.failCause(storedCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
export const sequential = Effect.failCause(Cause.sequential(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))
export const parallelLazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.parallel(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the constructed cause is transformed before being failed with
export const transformed = Effect.failCause(Cause.map(Cause.fail(error), (e) => e._tag))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Cause.fail and Effect.failCause are not adjacent in the flow
export const nonAdjacent = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Cause.map((e) => e._tag), Effect.failCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Cause constructors have no single-call Effect equivalent here
export const interrupted = Effect.failCause(Cause.interrupt(FiberId.none))
export const emptyCause = Effect.failCause(Cause.empty)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: type assertion on the argument changes the inferred error type
export const asserted = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error) as Cause.Cause<AppError | string>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type argument on failCause; with Cause.die it widens the
// error channel, which Effect.die(x) would not preserve
export const outerTypeArgumentDie = Effect.failCause<AppError>(Cause.die(defect))
export const outerTypeArgumentFail = Effect.failCause<AppError | string>(Cause.fail(error))
export const outerTypeArgumentPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause<AppError>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: return type annotation on the thunk pins the cause type
export const annotatedThunk = Effect.failCauseSync((): Cause.Cause<AppError | string> => Cause.fail(error))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause
export const lazyForwarded = Effect.failCauseSync(() => cause)
export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk does more than return the constructed cause
export const lazyMultiStatement = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  log("failing")
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: failCause of other modules (Exit, Stream, Channel) is not Effect.failCause
export const exitFailCause = Exit.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const streamFailCause = Stream.failCause(Cause.die(defect))
export const channelFailCause = Channel.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined APIs with the same names
const Local = {
  failCause: <E>(c: Cause.Cause<E>) => Effect.failCause(c),
  Cause: {
    fail: <E>(e: E): Cause.Cause<E> => Cause.fail(e),
    die: (d: unknown): Cause.Cause<never> => Cause.die(d)
  }
}
export const localFailCause = Local.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseFail = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseDie = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.die(defect))

// @effect-v3
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics failCauseToConstructor:warning
import * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import * as Channel from "effect/Channel"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Exit from "effect/Exit"
import * as FiberId from "effect/FiberId"
import { pipe } from "effect/Function"
import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"
import { die as causeDie, fail as causeFail } from "effect/Cause"
import { failCause, failCauseSync } from "effect/Effect"

class AppError {
  readonly _tag = "AppError"
}

declare const error: AppError
declare const defect: unknown
declare const cause: Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, AppError>
declare const compute: () => number
declare const makeCause: () => Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const log: (message: string) => void

// MUST TRIGGER: defect cause (issue example) -> Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const crashed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(new Error("boom")))

// MUST TRIGGER: typed failure cause (issue example) -> Effect.fail("not found" as const)
export const missing = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail("not found" as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy typed failure (issue example) -> Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))
export const lazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.fail(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier arguments -> Effect.fail(error) / Effect.die(defect)
export const failIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const dieIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST TRIGGER: side-effecting argument; both forms evaluate it eagerly -> Effect.die(compute())
export const dieComputed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(compute()))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect -> Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late")) (v3 has Effect.dieSync)
export const lazyDie = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyBlock = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: function-expression thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(function() { return error })
export const lazyFunction = Effect.failCauseSync(function() {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized inner constructor call -> Effect.fail(error)
export const parenthesized = Effect.failCause((Cause.fail(error)))

// MUST TRIGGER: explicit type argument on the inner constructor -> Effect.fail<AppError | string>(error)
export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: named imports resolve to the same APIs (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = failCauseSync(() => causeFail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: const alias of the API keeps its identity (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.fail(error))
const failCauseAlias = Effect.failCause
export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator
export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested in a function with an explicit Effect return type
export const withReturnType = (): Effect.Effect<never, AppError> => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: adjacent transformations in an existing flow -> Effect.fail(error)
export const transformationPair = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: replacing the flow prefix keeps later transformations
// -> pipe(Effect.die(defect), Effect.asVoid)
export const pipePrefix = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause, Effect.asVoid)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyFunctionPipe = pipe(() => Cause.fail(error), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.dieSync(() => defect)
export const lazyDiePipe = pipe(() => Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk body is itself a flow ending in Cause.fail -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyPipedBody = Effect.failCauseSync(() => pipe(error, Cause.fail))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already the direct APIs
export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const directFail = Effect.fail(error)
export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call
const storedCause = Cause.fail(error)
export const fromStoredCause = Effect.failCause(storedCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
export const sequential = Effect.failCause(Cause.sequential(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))
export const parallelLazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.parallel(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the constructed cause is transformed before being failed with
export const transformed = Effect.failCause(Cause.map(Cause.fail(error), (e) => e._tag))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Cause.fail and Effect.failCause are not adjacent in the flow
export const nonAdjacent = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Cause.map((e) => e._tag), Effect.failCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Cause constructors have no single-call Effect equivalent here
export const interrupted = Effect.failCause(Cause.interrupt(FiberId.none))
export const emptyCause = Effect.failCause(Cause.empty)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: type assertion on the argument changes the inferred error type
export const asserted = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error) as Cause.Cause<AppError | string>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type argument on failCause; with Cause.die it widens the
// error channel, which Effect.die(x) would not preserve
export const outerTypeArgumentDie = Effect.failCause<AppError>(Cause.die(defect))
export const outerTypeArgumentFail = Effect.failCause<AppError | string>(Cause.fail(error))
export const outerTypeArgumentPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause<AppError>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: return type annotation on the thunk pins the cause type
export const annotatedThunk = Effect.failCauseSync((): Cause.Cause<AppError | string> => Cause.fail(error))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause

export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause
export const lazyForwarded = Effect.failCauseSync(() => cause)
export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk does more than return the constructed cause
export const lazyMultiStatement = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  log("failing")
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: failCause of other modules (Exit, Stream, Channel) is not Effect.failCause
export const exitFailCause = Exit.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const streamFailCause = Stream.failCause(Cause.die(defect))
export const channelFailCause = Channel.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined APIs with the same names
const Local = {
  failCause: <E>(c: Cause.Cause<E>) => Effect.failCause(c),
  Cause: {
    fail: <E>(e: E): Cause.Cause<E> => Cause.fail(e),
    die: (d: unknown): Cause.Cause<never> => Cause.die(d)
  }
}
export const localFailCause = Local.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseFail = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseDie = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.die(defect))

// @effect-v3
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics failCauseToConstructor:warning
import * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import * as Channel from "effect/Channel"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Exit from "effect/Exit"
import * as FiberId from "effect/FiberId"
import { pipe } from "effect/Function"
import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"
import { die as causeDie, fail as causeFail } from "effect/Cause"
import { failCause, failCauseSync } from "effect/Effect"

class AppError {
  readonly _tag = "AppError"
}

declare const error: AppError
declare const defect: unknown
declare const cause: Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, AppError>
declare const compute: () => number
declare const makeCause: () => Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const log: (message: string) => void

// MUST TRIGGER: defect cause (issue example) -> Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const crashed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(new Error("boom")))

// MUST TRIGGER: typed failure cause (issue example) -> Effect.fail("not found" as const)
export const missing = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail("not found" as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy typed failure (issue example) -> Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))
export const lazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.fail(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier arguments -> Effect.fail(error) / Effect.die(defect)
export const failIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const dieIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST TRIGGER: side-effecting argument; both forms evaluate it eagerly -> Effect.die(compute())
export const dieComputed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(compute()))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect -> Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late")) (v3 has Effect.dieSync)
export const lazyDie = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyBlock = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: function-expression thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(function() { return error })
export const lazyFunction = Effect.failCauseSync(function() {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized inner constructor call -> Effect.fail(error)
export const parenthesized = Effect.fail(error)

// MUST TRIGGER: explicit type argument on the inner constructor -> Effect.fail<AppError | string>(error)
export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: named imports resolve to the same APIs (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = failCauseSync(() => causeFail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: const alias of the API keeps its identity (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.fail(error))
const failCauseAlias = Effect.failCause
export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator
export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested in a function with an explicit Effect return type
export const withReturnType = (): Effect.Effect<never, AppError> => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: adjacent transformations in an existing flow -> Effect.fail(error)
export const transformationPair = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: replacing the flow prefix keeps later transformations
// -> pipe(Effect.die(defect), Effect.asVoid)
export const pipePrefix = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause, Effect.asVoid)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyFunctionPipe = pipe(() => Cause.fail(error), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.dieSync(() => defect)
export const lazyDiePipe = pipe(() => Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk body is itself a flow ending in Cause.fail -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyPipedBody = Effect.failCauseSync(() => pipe(error, Cause.fail))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already the direct APIs
export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const directFail = Effect.fail(error)
export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call
const storedCause = Cause.fail(error)
export const fromStoredCause = Effect.failCause(storedCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
export const sequential = Effect.failCause(Cause.sequential(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))
export const parallelLazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.parallel(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the constructed cause is transformed before being failed with
export const transformed = Effect.failCause(Cause.map(Cause.fail(error), (e) => e._tag))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Cause.fail and Effect.failCause are not adjacent in the flow
export const nonAdjacent = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Cause.map((e) => e._tag), Effect.failCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Cause constructors have no single-call Effect equivalent here
export const interrupted = Effect.failCause(Cause.interrupt(FiberId.none))
export const emptyCause = Effect.failCause(Cause.empty)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: type assertion on the argument changes the inferred error type
export const asserted = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error) as Cause.Cause<AppError | string>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type argument on failCause; with Cause.die it widens the
// error channel, which Effect.die(x) would not preserve
export const outerTypeArgumentDie = Effect.failCause<AppError>(Cause.die(defect))
export const outerTypeArgumentFail = Effect.failCause<AppError | string>(Cause.fail(error))
export const outerTypeArgumentPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause<AppError>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: return type annotation on the thunk pins the cause type
export const annotatedThunk = Effect.failCauseSync((): Cause.Cause<AppError | string> => Cause.fail(error))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause
export const lazyForwarded = Effect.failCauseSync(() => cause)
export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk does more than return the constructed cause
export const lazyMultiStatement = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  log("failing")
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: failCause of other modules (Exit, Stream, Channel) is not Effect.failCause
export const exitFailCause = Exit.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const streamFailCause = Stream.failCause(Cause.die(defect))
export const channelFailCause = Channel.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined APIs with the same names
const Local = {
  failCause: <E>(c: Cause.Cause<E>) => Effect.failCause(c),
  Cause: {
    fail: <E>(e: E): Cause.Cause<E> => Cause.fail(e),
    die: (d: unknown): Cause.Cause<never> => Cause.die(d)
  }
}
export const localFailCause = Local.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseFail = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseDie = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.die(defect))

// @effect-v3
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics failCauseToConstructor:warning
import * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import * as Channel from "effect/Channel"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"

import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"

import { failCause, failCauseSync } from "effect/Effect"

class AppError {
  readonly _tag = "AppError"
}

declare const error: AppError
declare const defect: unknown
declare const cause: Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, AppError>
declare const compute: () => number
declare const makeCause: () => Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const log: (message: string) => void

// MUST TRIGGER: defect cause (issue example) -> Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const crashed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(new Error("boom")))

// MUST TRIGGER: typed failure cause (issue example) -> Effect.fail("not found" as const)
export const missing = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail("not found" as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy typed failure (issue example) -> Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))
export const lazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.fail(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier arguments -> Effect.fail(error) / Effect.die(defect)
export const failIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const dieIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST TRIGGER: side-effecting argument; both forms evaluate it eagerly -> Effect.die(compute())
export const dieComputed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(compute()))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect -> Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late")) (v3 has Effect.dieSync)
export const lazyDie = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyBlock = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: function-expression thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(function() { return error })
export const lazyFunction = Effect.failCauseSync(function() {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized inner constructor call -> Effect.fail(error)
export const parenthesized = Effect.failCause((Cause.fail(error)))

// MUST TRIGGER: explicit type argument on the inner constructor -> Effect.fail<AppError | string>(error)
export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: named imports resolve to the same APIs (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = Effect.failSync(() => error)

// MUST TRIGGER: const alias of the API keeps its identity (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.fail(error))
const failCauseAlias = Effect.failCause
export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator
export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested in a function with an explicit Effect return type
export const withReturnType = (): Effect.Effect<never, AppError> => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: adjacent transformations in an existing flow -> Effect.fail(error)
export const transformationPair = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: replacing the flow prefix keeps later transformations
// -> pipe(Effect.die(defect), Effect.asVoid)
export const pipePrefix = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause, Effect.asVoid)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyFunctionPipe = pipe(() => Cause.fail(error), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.dieSync(() => defect)
export const lazyDiePipe = pipe(() => Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk body is itself a flow ending in Cause.fail -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyPipedBody = Effect.failCauseSync(() => pipe(error, Cause.fail))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already the direct APIs
export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const directFail = Effect.fail(error)
export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call
const storedCause = Cause.fail(error)
export const fromStoredCause = Effect.failCause(storedCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
export const sequential = Effect.failCause(Cause.sequential(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))
export const parallelLazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.parallel(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the constructed cause is transformed before being failed with
export const transformed = Effect.failCause(Cause.map(Cause.fail(error), (e) => e._tag))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Cause.fail and Effect.failCause are not adjacent in the flow
export const nonAdjacent = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Cause.map((e) => e._tag), Effect.failCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Cause constructors have no single-call Effect equivalent here
export const interrupted = Effect.failCause(Cause.interrupt(FiberId.none))
export const emptyCause = Effect.failCause(Cause.empty)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: type assertion on the argument changes the inferred error type
export const asserted = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error) as Cause.Cause<AppError | string>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type argument on failCause; with Cause.die it widens the
// error channel, which Effect.die(x) would not preserve
export const outerTypeArgumentDie = Effect.failCause<AppError>(Cause.die(defect))
export const outerTypeArgumentFail = Effect.failCause<AppError | string>(Cause.fail(error))
export const outerTypeArgumentPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause<AppError>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: return type annotation on the thunk pins the cause type
export const annotatedThunk = Effect.failCauseSync((): Cause.Cause<AppError | string> => Cause.fail(error))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause
export const lazyForwarded = Effect.failCauseSync(() => cause)
export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk does more than return the constructed cause
export const lazyMultiStatement = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  log("failing")
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: failCause of other modules (Exit, Stream, Channel) is not Effect.failCause
export const exitFailCause = Exit.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const streamFailCause = Stream.failCause(Cause.die(defect))
export const channelFailCause = Channel.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined APIs with the same names
const Local = {
  failCause: <E>(c: Cause.Cause<E>) => Effect.failCause(c),
  Cause: {
    fail: <E>(e: E): Cause.Cause<E> => Cause.fail(e),
    die: (d: unknown): Cause.Cause<never> => Cause.die(d)
  }
}
export const localFailCause = Local.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseFail = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseDie = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.die(defect))

export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = failCauseSync(() => causeFail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: const alias of the API keeps its identity (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.fail(error))
const failCauseAlias = Effect.failCause
export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator
export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.fail(error))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested in a function with an explicit Effect return type
export const withReturnType = (): Effect.Effect<never, AppError> => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: adjacent transformations in an existing flow -> Effect.fail(error)
export const transformationPair = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: replacing the flow prefix keeps later transformations
// -> pipe(Effect.die(defect), Effect.asVoid)
export const pipePrefix = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause, Effect.asVoid)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyFunctionPipe = pipe(() => Cause.fail(error), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.dieSync(() => defect)
export const lazyDiePipe = pipe(() => Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk body is itself a flow ending in Cause.fail -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyPipedBody = Effect.failCauseSync(() => pipe(error, Cause.fail))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already the direct APIs
export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const directFail = Effect.fail(error)
export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call
const storedCause = Cause.fail(error)
export const fromStoredCause = Effect.failCause(storedCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
export const sequential = Effect.failCause(Cause.sequential(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))
export const parallelLazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.parallel(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the constructed cause is transformed before being failed with
export const transformed = Effect.failCause(Cause.map(Cause.fail(error), (e) => e._tag))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Cause.fail and Effect.failCause are not adjacent in the flow
export const nonAdjacent = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Cause.map((e) => e._tag), Effect.failCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Cause constructors have no single-call Effect equivalent here
export const interrupted = Effect.failCause(Cause.interrupt(FiberId.none))
export const emptyCause = Effect.failCause(Cause.empty)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: type assertion on the argument changes the inferred error type
export const asserted = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error) as Cause.Cause<AppError | string>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type argument on failCause; with Cause.die it widens the
// error channel, which Effect.die(x) would not preserve
export const outerTypeArgumentDie = Effect.failCause<AppError>(Cause.die(defect))
export const outerTypeArgumentFail = Effect.failCause<AppError | string>(Cause.fail(error))
export const outerTypeArgumentPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause<AppError>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: return type annotation on the thunk pins the cause type
export const annotatedThunk = Effect.failCauseSync((): Cause.Cause<AppError | string> => Cause.fail(error))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause
export const lazyForwarded = Effect.failCauseSync(() => cause)
export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk does more than return the constructed cause
export const lazyMultiStatement = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  log("failing")
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: failCause of other modules (Exit, Stream, Channel) is not Effect.failCause
export const exitFailCause = Exit.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const streamFailCause = Stream.failCause(Cause.die(defect))
export const channelFailCause = Channel.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined APIs with the same names
const Local = {
  failCause: <E>(c: Cause.Cause<E>) => Effect.failCause(c),
  Cause: {
    fail: <E>(e: E): Cause.Cause<E> => Cause.fail(e),
    die: (d: unknown): Cause.Cause<never> => Cause.die(d)
  }
}
export const localFailCause = Local.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseFail = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseDie = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.die(defect))

// @effect-v3
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics failCauseToConstructor:warning
import * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import * as Channel from "effect/Channel"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Exit from "effect/Exit"
import * as FiberId from "effect/FiberId"
import { pipe } from "effect/Function"
import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"
import { die as causeDie, fail as causeFail } from "effect/Cause"
import { failCause, failCauseSync } from "effect/Effect"

class AppError {
  readonly _tag = "AppError"
}

declare const error: AppError
declare const defect: unknown
declare const cause: Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, AppError>
declare const compute: () => number
declare const makeCause: () => Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const log: (message: string) => void

// MUST TRIGGER: defect cause (issue example) -> Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const crashed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(new Error("boom")))

// MUST TRIGGER: typed failure cause (issue example) -> Effect.fail("not found" as const)
export const missing = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail("not found" as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy typed failure (issue example) -> Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))
export const lazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.fail(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier arguments -> Effect.fail(error) / Effect.die(defect)
export const failIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const dieIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST TRIGGER: side-effecting argument; both forms evaluate it eagerly -> Effect.die(compute())
export const dieComputed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(compute()))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect -> Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late")) (v3 has Effect.dieSync)
export const lazyDie = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyBlock = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: function-expression thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(function() { return error })
export const lazyFunction = Effect.failCauseSync(function() {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized inner constructor call -> Effect.fail(error)
export const parenthesized = Effect.failCause((Cause.fail(error)))

// MUST TRIGGER: explicit type argument on the inner constructor -> Effect.fail<AppError | string>(error)
export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: named imports resolve to the same APIs (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = failCauseSync(() => causeFail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: const alias of the API keeps its identity (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.fail(error))
const failCauseAlias = Effect.failCause
export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator
export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested in a function with an explicit Effect return type
export const withReturnType = (): Effect.Effect<never, AppError> => Effect.fail(error)

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: adjacent transformations in an existing flow -> Effect.fail(error)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already the direct APIs
export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const directFail = Effect.fail(error)
export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call
const storedCause = Cause.fail(error)
export const fromStoredCause = Effect.failCause(storedCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
export const sequential = Effect.failCause(Cause.sequential(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))
export const parallelLazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.parallel(Cause.fail(error), Cause.die(defect)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the constructed cause is transformed before being failed with
export const transformed = Effect.failCause(Cause.map(Cause.fail(error), (e) => e._tag))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Cause.fail and Effect.failCause are not adjacent in the flow
export const nonAdjacent = pipe(error, Cause.fail, Cause.map((e) => e._tag), Effect.failCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Cause constructors have no single-call Effect equivalent here
export const interrupted = Effect.failCause(Cause.interrupt(FiberId.none))
export const emptyCause = Effect.failCause(Cause.empty)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: type assertion on the argument changes the inferred error type
export const asserted = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error) as Cause.Cause<AppError | string>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type argument on failCause; with Cause.die it widens the
// error channel, which Effect.die(x) would not preserve
export const outerTypeArgumentDie = Effect.failCause<AppError>(Cause.die(defect))
export const outerTypeArgumentFail = Effect.failCause<AppError | string>(Cause.fail(error))
export const outerTypeArgumentPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause<AppError>)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: return type annotation on the thunk pins the cause type
export const annotatedThunk = Effect.failCauseSync((): Cause.Cause<AppError | string> => Cause.fail(error))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk returns a forwarded or prebuilt cause
export const lazyForwarded = Effect.failCauseSync(() => cause)
export const lazyPointFree = Effect.failCauseSync(makeCause)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: thunk does more than return the constructed cause
export const lazyMultiStatement = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  log("failing")
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: failCause of other modules (Exit, Stream, Channel) is not Effect.failCause
export const exitFailCause = Exit.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const streamFailCause = Stream.failCause(Cause.die(defect))
export const channelFailCause = Channel.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined APIs with the same names
const Local = {
  failCause: <E>(c: Cause.Cause<E>) => Effect.failCause(c),
  Cause: {
    fail: <E>(e: E): Cause.Cause<E> => Cause.fail(e),
    die: (d: unknown): Cause.Cause<never> => Cause.die(d)
  }
}
export const localFailCause = Local.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseFail = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.fail(error))
export const localCauseDie = Effect.failCause(Local.Cause.die(defect))

// @effect-v3
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics failCauseToConstructor:warning
import * as Cause from "effect/Cause"
import * as Channel from "effect/Channel"
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect"
import * as Exit from "effect/Exit"
import * as FiberId from "effect/FiberId"
import { pipe } from "effect/Function"
import * as Stream from "effect/Stream"
import { die as causeDie, fail as causeFail } from "effect/Cause"
import { failCause, failCauseSync } from "effect/Effect"

class AppError {
  readonly _tag = "AppError"
}

declare const error: AppError
declare const defect: unknown
declare const cause: Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, AppError>
declare const compute: () => number
declare const makeCause: () => Cause.Cause<AppError>
declare const log: (message: string) => void

// MUST TRIGGER: defect cause (issue example) -> Effect.die(new Error("boom"))
export const crashed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(new Error("boom")))

// MUST TRIGGER: typed failure cause (issue example) -> Effect.fail("not found" as const)
export const missing = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail("not found" as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy typed failure (issue example) -> Effect.failSync(() => new Error("late"))
export const lazy = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.fail(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier arguments -> Effect.fail(error) / Effect.die(defect)
export const failIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
export const dieIdentifier = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(defect))

// MUST TRIGGER: side-effecting argument; both forms evaluate it eagerly -> Effect.die(compute())
export const dieComputed = Effect.failCause(Cause.die(compute()))

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect -> Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late")) (v3 has Effect.dieSync)
export const lazyDie = Effect.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(new Error("late")))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyBlock = Effect.failCauseSync(() => {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: function-expression thunk with a single return -> Effect.failSync(function() { return error })
export const lazyFunction = Effect.failCauseSync(function() {
  return Cause.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized inner constructor call -> Effect.fail(error)
export const parenthesized = Effect.failCause((Cause.fail(error)))

// MUST TRIGGER: explicit type argument on the inner constructor -> Effect.fail<AppError | string>(error)
export const innerTypeArgument = Effect.failCause(Cause.fail<AppError | string>(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: named imports resolve to the same APIs (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.die(defect) / Effect.failSync(() => error))
export const namedImports = failCause(causeDie(defect))
export const namedImportsLazy = failCauseSync(() => causeFail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: const alias of the API keeps its identity (report; the fix falls back to the
// file's Effect module identifier -> Effect.fail(error))
const failCauseAlias = Effect.failCause
export const aliasedCallee = failCauseAlias(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a generator
export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a pipeline callback
export const inPipe = pipe(
  Effect.succeed(1),
  Effect.flatMap(() => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested in a function with an explicit Effect return type
export const withReturnType = (): Effect.Effect<never, AppError> => Effect.failCause(Cause.fail(error))

// MUST TRIGGER: method-pipe form -> Effect.fail(error)
export const methodPipe = Cause.fail(error).pipe(Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: Function.pipe form -> Effect.die(defect)
export const functionPipe = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause)

// MUST TRIGGER: adjacent transformations in an existing flow -> Effect.fail(error)
export const transformationPair = Effect.fail(error)

// MUST TRIGGER: replacing the flow prefix keeps later transformations
// -> pipe(Effect.die(defect), Effect.asVoid)
export const pipePrefix = pipe(Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCause, Effect.asVoid)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyFunctionPipe = pipe(() => Cause.fail(error), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: lazy defect thunk as the subject of a Function.pipe flow -> Effect.dieSync(() => defect)
export const lazyDiePipe = pipe(() => Cause.die(defect), Effect.failCauseSync)

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk body is itself a flow ending in Cause.fail -> Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const lazyPipedBody = Effect.failCauseSync(() => pipe(error, Cause.fail))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already the direct APIs
export const directDie = Effect.die(new Error("boom"))

export const directFailSync = Effect.failSync(() => error)
export const directDieSync = Effect.dieSync(() => new Error("late"))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: forwarded cause (dominant real-world usage)
export const forwarded = Effect.failCause(cause)
export const forwardedFromExit = Exit.isFailure(exit) ? Effect.failCause(exit.cause) : Effect.void

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a cause stored in a variable first is a forwarded cause, not a direct call

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: composed causes
